features.name: Transaction control in AL runtime
features.description: The AL runtime automatically manages database transactions - it opens a write transaction on the first insert, modify, or delete operation and commits implicitly when code execution ends without error. Developers cannot manually start transactions like in SQL; instead, explicit commits split transactions into separate units.

features.name: Rollback scope limitations
features.description: Rollback undoes only inserts, modifies, and deletes on normal tables since the last commit. It does not undo: variables, temporary records, single instance codeunit state, HTTP calls, sent emails, or telemetry. This asymmetry can lead to partial state inconsistencies.
caveats: Variables retain their values even after rollback
Temporary records are not rolled back
External system calls are not undone

features.name: Explicit commit splitting transactions
features.description: When a developer places an explicit Commit in code, it finalizes all database writes up to that point into a separate transaction. Subsequent writes become part of a new transaction. This allows intentional transaction splitting but can create data consistency issues if errors occur after the commit.
caveats: Commits split transactions, not create new ones
Early commits can leave data inconsistent if later code fails

features.name: The rollback that wasn't - try-catch with database writes
features.description: When an error is caught inside a try-catch block, the database modifications made before the error are not automatically rolled back in online Business Central. This means a try-catch block can leave the database in a partially modified state even though an error occurred and was handled. On premises, writes inside try methods are blocked by default.
caveats: Behavior differs between online and on-premises
On-premises blocks writes in try methods
Online allows writes to persist even when error is caught

features.name: Try function error handling
features.description: Try functions catch errors but do not undo writes that occurred within the try block. Catching an error is not the same as undoing the write transaction.
caveats: Online Business Central allows writes in try methods; on-premises blocks them by default
Behavior differs between online and on-premises deployments

features.name: Commit method behavior
features.description: The Commit method makes everything written since the last commit final, including writes from the current method, callers, and all subscriber rights. It releases locks and opens a new transaction.
caveats: Every commit creates a state someone must be able to recover from
Defensive commits can lead to inconsistent data

features.name: Outbox pattern for external integration
features.description: A pattern that saves to a send queue/outbox table instead of directly posting to external systems. The outbox entries are processed after commit by job queue, making retries safe from duplicate exports.
caveats: External calls cannot be undone by database rollback
HTTP calls inside write transactions hold locks on the whole call duration

features.name: Idempotent request IDs
features.description: Using stable IDs like system ID on every request to allow external systems to ignore requests they have already seen, preventing duplicate processing.

features.name: External Business Events post-commit behavior
features.description: External business events in Business Central go out only after the commit and never after rollback, ensuring consistency with database state.

features.name: Batch checkpoint pattern
features.description: A pattern where batch processing saves progress in a table within the same transaction as the work, allowing safe recovery on failure. Progress is committed together with processed data.
caveats: Progress must be tracked in a table, not in memory
Each commit needs a comment explaining why everything before it is final

features.name: Commit Behavior function attribute
features.description: A procedure or event attribute that controls transaction commit behavior in AL code. Supports four rules: ignore does nothing, error raises an error, covers the method and all calls until exit, and stricter parent behavior overrides child ignore.
features.status_evidence_quote: Microsoft ships this in base app. Sales post runs the posting lines under commit behavior ignore by default, at least in BC 29.
caveats: Attribute cannot be conditional
Applies only in scope of commit behavior procedure

features.name: Error-scoped Code Units for clean state transactions
features.description: Code units that run with their own transaction boundary using the return value pattern, creating a scoped undo mechanism. Requires clean state - no existing write transactions before calling.
caveats: Must be in clean state - cannot have open write transactions
Runtime enforces this restriction
Compiler does not enforce it
Only works with return value - without it is ordinary call

features.name: Try function attribute with return value
features.description: Attribute for procedures that catches errors without rolling back database changes made by try methods. Changes are committed. Allows writing in online, but disabled by default on premises.
caveats: Only creates a boundary when return value is used
Bare calls are ordinary calls where errors propagate
Behavior might change in upcoming release per documentation
Writes are not rolled back unlike error-scoped code units

features.name: Test transaction models
features.description: Test code units can specify transaction behavior via attribute: After Rollback (changes roll back, commits cause error), After Commit (changes persist, runners clean up), None (test cannot write, page interactions commit like real client).
caveats: Default is auto commit
Under auto commit and auto rollback, triggers inherit test open transactions
Should match the code under test

features.name: Test transaction model - after rollback
features.description: Test transaction model option where everything rolls back at the end of the test and a call to commit causes an error. Used when code never commits.

features.name: Test transaction model - after commit
features.description: Test transaction model option where changes persist and the runner's test isolation cleans up. Used when code commits, for posting, job queues, integrations.

features.name: Test transaction model - none
features.description: Test transaction model option where the test itself can't write and each page interaction commits on its own, like a real client. Used for UI and read-only tests.

features.name: Error info data type
features.description: A data type that lets you build detailed errors with properties like message, detailed message, title, error type, verbosity, data classification, custom dimensions, and fix-it handler. Supports context information like record ID, system ID, table ID, field number, page number, control name.
caveats: method name in fix-it handler is plain text and type checking fails only at runtime

features.name: Fix-it actions in error dialog
features.description: Error dialogs can carry two kinds of actions: show-it which adds navigation action with page number, record ID, and field number to open the right page on the right field; and fix-it which adds action with a codeunit and method name.
caveats: fix-it method name type checking fails at runtime only

features.name: Error behavior collect
features.description: A tool for procedures that run and check items. Inside it, collectible errors are gathered and execution keeps going. At the end, unhandled errors become one error and transaction rolls back. Non-collectible errors stop execution at once.
caveats: get collected errors doesn't clear the list
clearing collected errors doesn't roll back database changes

features.name: Collectible errors in error info
features.description: Error info.create with no arguments is collectible by default. With a message, the collectible flag is optional and should be set explicitly.

features.name: Free show-it feature since BC 24
features.description: Available since Business Central 24 where the single parameter test field at a source action is added automatically for show-it actions, unless the test field already has a value.
caveats: if test field has a value already, it will not add it

features.name: Transaction Handling Checklist
features.description: Eight-item code review checklist for transaction management including no insert/modify/delete in try functions, error logging after rollback, and proper use of if-codeunit-run.

features.name: Try Function Behavior: On-Premise vs Online
features.description: Explains that try function behavior differs between on-premise and Business Central online: on-premise throws runtime error for writes in try, while online allows writes but does not undo them on error.
caveats: Controlled by NST service tier settings
On-premise allows changing the setting; online does not
